messages.subject: R RpostgreSQL bigint datatype issue
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Could anybody advise what is the best solution to read/write big int values 
via RpostgreSQL?
I have an unique identifier field which contains numbers like: 212982, 
212983,1380742793415240,1380742793415241
The latter two are being send to database using scientific notation, and by 
default when using dbWriteTable they are written to db as double precision 
- which makes both of them identical, therefore not able to use as primary 
key.

I prefer to not store them as character because I would need to fill the 
shorter values with leading zeros to have exact nchar() to be able to query 
using >, >= operators on character fields.
The performance is a factor in the process, currently table has 6 million 
rows but is going to be double every year, I'm not aware of postgresql 
performance when using text_field >= '000212982' but I assume that numbers 
could be faster.

What is the most effective way to process that case??

While reading the documentation: 
http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/RPostgreSQL/RPostgreSQL.pdf
I see there seems to be function dbSetDataMappings - as per doc it is not 
yet implemented.
Maybe there is some draft in the background of package I would use to map 
that column to postgresql bigint datatype?
Any other way?

Thanks

--

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Write as characters and convert to bigint inside PostgreSQL seems to work in the example you have shown.
> library(RPostgreSQL)
Loading required package: DBI
> c=dbConnect("PostgreSQL")
> a <- 1380742793415240
> b <- 1380742793415241
> dc <-data.frame(a=as.character(a), b=as.character(b))
> dbWriteTable(c,"testclosenumberch", dc)
[1] TRUE
> dbGetQuery(c, "select * from testclosenumberch")
  row.names                a                b
1         1 1380742793415240 1380742793415241
> dbGetQuery(c, "select a::bigint - b::bigint  from testclosenumberch")
  ?column?
1       -1

In this example, only a simple select example is shown, but you can select into a new
table just after dbWriteTable if you the performance for query is more important than
the storing the data.

However, note that numeric value in R itself is just a double precision
floating point number having 53 significant bits, which is shorter than 64 bits.

--

messages.subject: Bug in postgresql
messages.body_plain:
setMethod("print", "dbObjectId",
          def = function(x, ...){
              expired <- if(isPostgresqlIdCurrent(x)) "" else "Expired "
              str <- paste("<", expired, class(x), ":", format(x), ">", 
sep="")
              cat(str, "\n")
              invisible(NULL)
          }
)

Here you're tying the method for an object that underlies all of DBI to a 
postgresql specific implementation.

This ends up causing RMySQL to fail if you have RSQLite, RMySQL and 
RPostgreSQL loaded simultaneously.

I think you should really only create methods on classes that declare, so 
this should be:

setMethod("print", "PostgreSQLDriver",
          def = function(x, ...){
              expired <- if(isPostgresqlIdCurrent(x)) "" else "Expired "
              str <- paste("<", expired, class(x), ":", format(x), ">", 
sep="")
              cat(str, "\n")
              invisible(NULL)
          }
)

and similar for every other method in dbObject

Hadley

After you load the data just execute the following SQL:

ALTER TABLE test_1 ADD COLUMN my_id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY;

where test_1 is the table name and my_id is the name of the id column you which to add.

BIGSERIAL should be used if you anticipate the use of more than 2^31 identifiers over the lifetime of the table.

Neil

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I similarly am bridging R and psql, wish to remove vulnerability to sql 
injection.  Looking at documentation, I had hoped that:

postgresqlExecStatement(con, statement, params, ...)

Would allow use of something like:

postgresqlExecStatement(con, "DELETE FROM ? WHERE id = ?", c("foo_bar", 1))

But unfortunately this does not seem to work.  Maybe I'm using the wrong 
symbol for parameter (something other than ?).

Best compromise I've found is escaping strings via:

postgresqlEscapeStrings(con, string)

connection is necessary so function can know how to properly escape.

Means I have to escape every string I use in a paste when putting together 
my queries.  Not so elegant.  But seems best option.  Anyone have other 
ideas?

Thanks,
PGS

Hi,

PostgreSQL uses $1, $2, $3, ... for the parameter.

> postgresqlExecStatement(con, "DELETE FROM ? WHERE id = ?", c("foo_bar", 1))


You might try:
postgresqlExecStatement(con, "DELETE FROM $1 WHERE id = $2", c("foo_bar", 1))
